Question Choices: Select. A rectangle and a parallelogram both have base 5 cm and height 4 cm. Which has a larger area?: ~~rectangle | parallelogram | same-area~~
Solution: Both area formulas are base × perpendicular height. Each gives 5×4=20 cm², so the areas are the same.

Question Choices: A parallelogram has area 63 cm² and height 9 cm. Find the base. (Just put the values, no units needed)
Hints: Divide area by the known base or perpendicular height.
Solution: A=bh. Divide the area by the known dimension: base=63/9=7 cm. Check: 9×7=63 cm².

Question Choices: Select. A parallelogram has area 42 cm². The base is 7 cm. A student says the height is 8 cm. Is the student correct?: ~~Correct | Wrong~~
Hints: Check the claim by multiplying base and height.
Solution: The claimed height gives 7×8=56 cm², not 42. The correct height is 42/7=6 cm.

Question Choices: Parallelograms A and B have the same area (72 cm²). A has base 12 cm. B has base 8 cm. Find both heights. (Just put the values, no units needed) Height of A: ___ cm. Height of B: ___ cm.
Hints: Use the same area with each different base.
Solution: h=A/b. Height A=72/12=6 cm; height B=72/8=9 cm. Check: 12×6=8×9=72.

Question Choices: Select. A parallelogram and a rectangle have the same base and height. Why do they have the same area? (A) Because both shapes have four sides (B) Because the slanted sides of a parallelogram are equal to the rectangle's sides (C) Because you can cut and move part of the parallelogram to form a rectangle without changing the area (D) Because a parallelogram is always a rectangle: ~~A | B | C | D~~
Hints: Think about preserving all the pieces while making a rectangle.
Solution: Cut and translate pieces to make a rectangle with the same base and perpendicular height, with no gaps or overlap. Moving the pieces adds or removes no area. Four sides alone do not determine area; a parallelogram need not be a rectangle. Therefore C.
